# fcoding — shared contract (server <-> UI). Architect-owned; workers do not edit.

Goal: a mobile web app (PWA, iOS 16.7 Safari, iPhone X) to chat with coding harnesses (omp, claude, codex, shell) running in tmux sessions on instabox box `coder`, reached through a PUBLIC instabox URL (`instabox port publish coder 7681`). Vietnamese typing must be exact: text is typed in a native <textarea>, sent as UTF-8, and pasted into tmux as one block.

Files (one owner each):
- server.mjs — Node 22, built-ins only (no npm deps). Owner: sonnet-executor.
- public/index.html (+ inline CSS/JS), public/manifest.webmanifest, public/icon.svg — Owner: frontend-implementor.
- test/server.test.mjs — Owner: sonnet-executor.
- install.sh (box install + systemd --user unit) — Owner: sonnet-executor.

Runtime on the box: /data/home/fcoding/server.mjs. Config dir /data/home/.fcoding/ (mode 700): config.json (mode 600) holds { passwordHash (scrypt, salt, N/r/p), cookieSecret, projects: {name: absDir}, port: 7681 }. `node server.mjs --set-password` reads a password from stdin (or generates a random 24-char one and prints it ONCE) and writes the hash. Listen 0.0.0.0:7681 (only reachable through the instabox proxy).

Security invariants (must hold; Astra High reviews them):
S1 Every route except GET /, /index.html, /manifest.webmanifest, /icon.svg, POST /api/login requires a valid session cookie.
S2 Login: scrypt verify, constant-time compare; rate limit 5 failures / 15 min per client IP (X-Forwarded-For first hop if present, else socket) AND a global limit of 30 failures / hour, both answering 429 with Retry-After; no user enumeration (single password).
S3 Session cookie `pc_sid`: 32 random bytes, HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Strict, Path=/, Max-Age 30 days; server stores only sha256(sid); logout and "log out everywhere" (POST /api/logout?all=1) revoke.
S4 CSRF: every POST requires header `X-PC: 1` and, when an Origin header is present, it must equal the request's own origin (Host + https); reject otherwise (403).
S5 Commands only through child_process.execFile('tmux', [...args]) — never a shell. Session names must match ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,31}$. Key names only from the KEYS whitelist below. Projects and harnesses only from config / HARNESSES.
S6 Body size limit 64 KB; text field max 32 KB; JSON only.
S7 Security headers on every response: Content-Security-Policy "default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; img-src 'self' data:; connect-src 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'", X-Content-Type-Options nosniff, Referrer-Policy no-referrer, Cache-Control no-store on /api/*.
S8 Never log passwords, cookies or sent text; log only method, path, status, ms.

HARNESSES (command run inside the tmux session, cwd = project dir): omp -> `omp`, claude -> `claude`, codex -> `codex`, shell -> `bash -l`. tmux sessions get env LANG=C.UTF-8 LC_ALL=C.UTF-8.
KEYS whitelist (tmux send-keys names): Enter, Escape, Tab, BTab, Up, Down, Left, Right, PageUp, PageDown, Home, End, BSpace, C-c, C-d, C-l, C-o, C-r, C-u, C-z, M-a, y, n, Space. (M-a = Alt+A opens the omp agent hub; C-o expands tool output (e.g. in an agent opened from the hub).)

API (JSON; errors as {error:"code"} with HTTP status):
- POST /api/login {password} -> 200 {ok:true} + Set-Cookie | 401 {error:"bad_password"} | 429 {error:"rate_limited", retryAfter:s}
- POST /api/logout[?all=1] -> 200 {ok:true}
- GET  /api/me -> 200 {ok:true} | 401
- GET  /api/meta -> {projects:[name...], harnesses:[...], keys:[...]}
- GET  /api/sessions -> {sessions:[{name, project|null, harness|null, created, attached:boolean, activity}]}
- POST /api/sessions {name, project, harness} -> 201 {name} | 409 {error:"exists"} | 400 {error:"invalid"}
- DELETE /api/sessions/:name -> 200 (kill-session) (needs X-PC header too)
- GET  /api/screen/:name?lines=N (N 50..2000, default 300) -> {text, rows, cols, cursor:{x,y}, hash} ; text = `tmux capture-pane -p -J -S -N` (plain text, no ANSI), trailing blank lines trimmed. Optional `?ansi=1` keeps SGR colours in `text` (see A6); also on /api/stream
- GET  /api/stream/:name -> text/event-stream; event "screen" with the same JSON whenever hash changes (poll tmux every 700 ms), comment ping every 15 s; ends on logout/session gone (event "gone")
- POST /api/send/:name {text, enter:boolean} -> 200; multi-line or long text uses `tmux load-buffer -b pc -` (stdin) + `tmux paste-buffer -p -d -b pc -t name` (bracketed paste); single line uses `send-keys -l -t name -- text`; then `send-keys Enter` if enter
- POST /api/key/:name {key, repeat?:1..20} -> 200 | 400 {error:"bad_key"}
- POST /api/resize/:name {cols, rows} (cols 20..300, rows 10..200) -> resize-window
Static: GET / serves public/index.html; manifest + icon.

UI requirements (frontend): Vietnamese labels; login screen; session list (create: name, project, harness; delete with confirm UI, not window.confirm); session view: monospace screen (auto-scroll unless user scrolled up; font-size A-/A+ saved in localStorage), SSE with reconnect + fallback polling, connection dot; bottom composer: <textarea> (Enter inserts newline; a big Gửi button sends with enter:true; a secondary "Gửi không Enter"), quick-key bar (Esc, Ctrl+C, ↑, ↓, ←, →, Tab, ⇧Tab, Enter, y, n, /) plus a "/lệnh" menu with common slash commands; send resize on load/orientation change computed from font metrics; iOS: apple-mobile-web-app-capable, viewport-fit=cover, safe-area insets, no zoom on focus (font-size >= 16px in textarea), works without any CDN; dark theme by default. Every fetch sends X-PC: 1 and credentials same-origin.

## Amendment A1 (2026-10-25): native iOS client replaces the web UI
- The client is a native SwiftUI app (folder ios/), not a web page. public/ is dropped: GET / returns a small plain-text "fcoding ok" (no auth needed); no static files, no manifest, no icon. The CSP header stays (harmless).
- Native client sends no Origin header: S4 still requires `X-PC: 1` on every POST/DELETE; Origin is checked only when present.
- Cookies: the app uses URLSession with HTTPCookieStorage (persistent). Login also returns the session id in the JSON body as {ok:true, token} ONLY when the request carries header `X-PC-Client: ios`; the server then also accepts `Authorization: Bearer <token>` as an alternative to the cookie (same sid store, same expiry, same revocation). Tokens are never logged.
- New route: POST /api/open {project, harness} -> 200 {name, created:boolean}. Session name = `<project>-<harness>` (sanitised to the name regex); if it exists, return it (created:false); else create it in the project dir with the harness command (created:true). This is the app's "quick open project" button.
- SSE (/api/stream/:name) must work for a non-browser client: send `retry: 3000`, flush each event immediately, no compression.

## Amendment A2 (2026-10-25): behind the instabox proxy, robustness
- Proxy facts (Architect probe): the instabox port proxy overwrites X-Forwarded-For with the real client IP, sends Host: 127.0.0.1:<port> and X-Forwarded-Proto: https, and normalises `//` to `/`. First-hop XFF is the client IP. Only the native app is a client; an Origin header, when present, must equal `https://` + (X-Forwarded-Host || Host), else 403 (browsers are not supported clients).
- /api/screen and SSE `cursor` are relative to the visible pane; `rows` is the visible pane height; `text` may include history above it (client maps y = lineCount - rows + cursor.y).
- Phone resize makes the window size manual; a laptop that attaches later runs `tmux resize-window -A` (documented in README).
- Fail closed: if sessions.json cannot be written, the server stops accepting any session (all protected routes 401) until a write succeeds; logout returns 500 in that case.
- Password change (`--set-password`) rotates cookieSecret; a running server notices the config change (mtime check before auth) and reloads the hash and secret, dropping all sessions immediately — no restart needed.
- Limits: at most 50 SSE streams (reserved before any await), at most 20 queued sends (503 {error:"busy"}), at most 8 concurrent tmux child processes; queued work for a closed request is cancelled.

## Amendment A3 (2026-10-25): simpler design after two failed rounds (supersedes conflicting parts of A2)
- Sessions live in MEMORY ONLY. There is no sessions.json. Any server restart logs out every device (the app shows login again). Revocation is therefore always durable. config.json is the only file; it holds passwordHash, cookieSecret, projects, port.
- Config: parse + validate a complete candidate before use; at startup an invalid/missing config refuses to start (exit 1); on reload failure keep the previous snapshot and retry on the next stamp change. --set-password writes hash + a rotated secret atomically (tmp, fsync, rename, dir fsync); a running server sees the new stamp, swaps config and drops all in-memory sessions. Strip only the trailing line ending from the stdin password.
- One execution gate for every tmux child: run(ctx, argv[, stdin]). ctx = {req, sid, gen}. After acquiring capacity and with no await before execFile, it re-checks: client not disconnected, session still valid and not expired, config generation unchanged; else it rejects without spawning. Every route passes ctx; there is no tmux call without ctx.
- Capacity: 8 child slots, 1 reserved for the active mutation. Reads (screen, SSE capture, sessions list, meta) take a free slot immediately or get 503 busy; reads never queue.
- Mutations (open, create, delete, send, key, resize) are whole jobs in ONE FIFO of at most 20 waiting jobs (overflow 503 busy), one active at a time. A multi-step job (paste then Enter; create then metadata; /api/open check-then-create) runs entirely inside its job, and every step goes through run(ctx). Disconnected jobs are removed promptly. Body is read (bounded) and auth re-checked after the body completes, before the job is queued. Auth/login/logout are not queued.
- SSE: auth check inside the guarded tick; no polling while paused; `last` advances only when the event is handed to write(); timers and the slot are released exactly once. `event: gone` carries data {"reason":"session"} or {"reason":"auth"}.
- Harness launch: the command runs as `env PATH=<HOME>/.local/bin:<HOME>/.bun/bin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin <harness>` (no reliance on the tmux server's or the unit's PATH). If the session is gone right after new-session, /api/open and POST /api/sessions return 500 {"error":"harness_exited"}. NOT_FOUND also matches "no such session".
- Screen trim: linear backward scan; removes only trailing blank lines.
- iOS: logout shows failure and offers retry; "Đăng xuất trên máy này" clears only local credentials, "Đăng xuất mọi nơi" clears locally only after the server confirms. On SSE gone with reason auth (or a 401 from /api/me) go to login; with reason session show "Phiên đã đóng".

## Amendment A4 (2026-10-25, user decision): device pairing replaces the password

- No password. Remove POST /api/login, passwordHash in the config, --set-password, scrypt and the login rate limiter. config.json keeps cookieSecret, projects and port.
- Only someone with a shell on the box can start a pairing.
  - The command is `node server.mjs --pair [device-name]`. install.sh also installs the wrapper `~/.local/bin/fcode-pair`, which runs it.
  - The CLI talks to the RUNNING server over the unix socket <configDir>/admin.sock. The socket has mode 600 and is usable by its owner only. The server creates it at start and removes a stale one.
  - The server creates a pending pairing code for the shell issuer. Its 6-digit code comes from crypto.randomInt. The code is valid for 120 s and allows at most 5 wrong attempts. The pending codes are per issuer (changed by A7: up to 3 in all); a new --pair replaces the shell's own code.
  - The CLI prints the code and the expiry time, then exits.
  - If the server is not running, the CLI says so and exits 1.
- POST /api/pair {code, name} requires X-PC: 1 and no other auth.
  - Success: 200 {ok:true, token} and Set-Cookie pc_sid, with the same flags as before.
  - Wrong or expired code: 401 {error:"bad_code"}. Five wrong attempts invalidate the pending code.
  - Global limit on /api/pair: 10 per minute and 30 per hour. Over the limit: 429 with Retry-After.
  - Codes are compared in constant time.
- Devices are stored in <configDir>/devices.json, mode 600.
  - Only the server writes the file, using the atomic write: tmp file, fsync, rename, directory fsync.
  - Format: {devices:[{id, name, keyHash: HMAC-SHA256(cookieSecret, token), createdAt}]}.
  - The token is returned once. It is never stored or logged.
  - A pairing succeeds only after the durable write succeeds. Otherwise: 500 {error:"storage"} and no token.
  - Devices survive server restarts. They do not expire; a device stays until it is revoked.
- Revocation:
  - `node server.mjs --devices` lists id, name and createdAt.
  - `--revoke <id>` and `--revoke all` go through admin.sock. The server writes devices.json first, then removes the device from memory and bumps gen for that device. In-flight jobs for that device stop at the gate.
  - If the write fails, the CLI prints the error and exits 1, and nothing changes.
  - POST /api/logout removes the calling device the same way. On failure: 500 storage.
  - POST /api/logout?all=1 removes all devices.
- Startup: if devices.json is missing, the device list is empty. If it is present but invalid, the server refuses to start: exit 1, with no secrets in the message.
- The run(ctx) gate checks that the device id still exists and gen is unchanged. This replaces the memory-session check.
- Rotating cookieSecret (a manual config edit) invalidates every device, because keyHash no longer matches. The server then rewrites devices.json as an empty list.
- Client (iOS): the token is stored in the Keychain. When the app is signed by Sideloadly, it has a normal keychain.

### A4 update r1 (2026-10-25, review round 1)
- Commit point = the rename of devices.json. After it succeeds, the change is committed: memory follows, a directory-fsync error is only logged (pair returns the token, revoke/logout succeed). A failure before or at the rename changes nothing (storage error).
- devices.json has `secretTag` = HMAC-SHA256(cookieSecret, "fcoding-devices") hex. At startup and on every config reload, a tag that does not match the current secret clears the devices from memory first, then rewrites devices.json empty with the new tag. If that rewrite fails, `purgePending` is set: the purge is retried before any other devices.json write, on every admin request and on each config refresh; meanwhile no device authenticates and pairing answers 500 storage. No tag + empty list = valid (first run); no tag + devices = mismatch.
- /api/pair counts against 10/min and 30/h before the body is read (oversized, slow and invalid bodies count too).
- parseDevices checks exact types (strings for id, name, keyHash, secretTag; number for createdAt) before any pattern check.
- admin.sock handles only the first line of a connection; admin() calls refreshConfig() first.
- The CLI prints the remaining time: "Mã ghép: 482913 (hết hạn sau 120 giây)".
- Device names lose C0, DEL, C1 (U+0080–U+009F) and bidi controls (U+200E/U+200F, U+202A–U+202E, U+2066–U+2069).
- install.sh quotes the paths in the fcode-pair wrapper and removes an obsolete passwordHash from config.json atomically (tmp, fsync, rename, mode 600; other fields kept).
- Accepted: anyone on the internet can use up the global 30/h pairing limit; the owner then waits up to 1 h.

### A4 update r3 (2026-10-25, review round 3: single instance; replaces every admin.sock probe)
- Instance lock first: before it loads config, devices or anything else, the server binds a Linux abstract-namespace unix socket used only as a lock, named NUL + "fcoding-lock-" + sha256(realpath(configDir)) hex, first 32 characters. EADDRINUSE means another live server owns this config dir: exit 1 with "Một máy chủ FCode khác đang dùng thư mục cấu hình này", touching nothing. The kernel frees the name when the process dies, so there is no stale lock. Nobody connects to it. Windows (local tests only): a named pipe with the same derived name.
- admin.sock: only the lock holder gets there. It unlinks any existing admin.sock and binds a new one (mode 600). There is no connect probe. A path that exists and is not a socket still refuses the start.
- Accepted trade-off: an abstract socket has no permissions, so another local user on the same box could hold the name and block a start, but could not take over the server. This is accepted because the box has a single user.

## Amendment A5 (2026-10-25, user decision): project list = attention-first inbox + harness dock
- New read endpoint GET /api/overview (auth like other reads; it goes through the read gate as ONE read job; internal tmux/git calls run sequentially inside that job, each with the existing exec timeout). Response:
  `{ now, projects: [{ name, branch, ahead, diff: {files, add, del} | null }], sessions: [{ name, project, harness, created, activity, attached, state, preview }] }`
  - `state`: "running" if session_activity is within 8 s of now; otherwise "waiting" if the last 6 non-empty lines of the visible pane match an approval/question pattern (case-insensitive: `(y/n)`, `[y/n]`, `[Y/n]`, `[y/N]`, `yes/no`, `do you want`, `allow`, `approve`, `proceed?`, `continue?`, `press enter`, a numbered choice line like `❯ 1.` or `> 1.`); otherwise "idle". The pattern list lives in one constant.
  - `preview`: the last non-empty pane line that is not prompt/box-drawing chrome, ANSI-stripped, control chars removed, trimmed, at most 160 chars (cut on a code-point boundary).
  - `branch`: `git -C <dir> rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD`; `diff`: from `git -C <dir> diff --shortstat HEAD` (null if not a git repo or on error); `ahead`: commits ahead of upstream or null. Git results are cached per project for 10 s.
  - Never include secrets or file contents beyond the preview line. Errors in one project/session give nulls for that item, not a failed response.
- Unread is client-side: the app stores the last `activity` it has seen per session.
- Inline answers use the existing POST /api/key and /api/send (e.g. send text "y" with enter).
- iOS: screen = inbox (header "FCode", subtitle "N phiên đang chờ bạn" when N>0, gear left, "+" right), project filter pills, sections "Cần bạn" (waiting; full preview + buttons: y/n prompts get "y · Đồng ý", "n · Từ chối", "Mở"; others "Trả lời", "Mở"), "Đang chạy" (project · branch · diff, one-line preview, thin activity bar), "Đang nghỉ" (compact, dimmed). Bottom: floating translucent harness dock (Tất cả / omp / claude / codex / shell, icon + label) filtering the list; "+" opens a sheet that skips the harness step when the dock has a harness selected. Poll /api/overview every 5 s while visible (pause in background), pull to refresh, swipe left on a row: "Đã đọc/Chưa đọc", "Xoá" (kill session with confirmation).
- A5 update (user, 2026-10-25): "Cần bạn" is always expanded. "Đang chạy" and "Đang nghỉ" are collapsed by default: one header row each (name, count, the harness badges of its sessions, chevron); tapping the row expands/collapses it with an animation. The expanded/collapsed state is remembered per section (UserDefaults). An empty section is hidden.
- A5 update 2 (user, 2026-10-25): the project filter row uses Cây A's chip rail instead of Cây B's pills: horizontal scrolling capsules "Tất cả", then each project; a chip shows an orange badge with the number of sessions waiting for the user, or a grey session count when none wait; the selected chip is white with dark text.
- A5 update 3 (user, 2026-10-25): harness colours — claude orange (#D97757), omp purple (#A78BFA), codex blue (#5AC8FA-like, as in the preview), shell grey. The codex glyph matches the official Codex mark (drawn as a vector, not a downloaded image).
- A5 update 4 (user, 2026-10-25): "+" always STARTS A NEW SESSION (it never reopens an old one; existing sessions are opened from the list). Server: POST /api/open accepts an optional `fresh: true`. With fresh, inside ONE mutation job the server picks the first free name among `<base>`, `<base>-2`, `<base>-3`, … (base = the existing project-harness name rule; the suffix is kept within the 32-char limit by shortening base) and creates it; it never reuses an existing session. Response `{name, created:true}`. Without fresh the old behaviour stays. iOS: the "+" sheet's project rows say "Phiên mới · đang có N phiên <harness>" (or "Phiên mới" when none) and call /api/open with fresh:true, then open the new session.
- A5 update 5 (2026-10-25): in /api/overview, `now`, `created` and `activity` are Unix epoch SECONDS (integers). When `state` is "waiting", `preview` is the question line: among the last 6 non-empty lines that match the approval/question pattern (cleaned the same way, at most 160 code points), the last one that is not a numbered option (`^[❯>›]?\s*\d+\.\s` after cleaning); if only numbered options match, the last of those. Example: "Do you want to proceed?" / "❯ 1. Yes" / "2. No" gives "Do you want to proceed?". So the client can detect y/n prompts from it; otherwise the existing preview rule applies. `activity` is the later of tmux `session_activity` and `window_activity` (tmux moves only window_activity on pane output), and `state` uses it.
- A5 update 6 (2026-10-25, final integration r3, option A): each overview session has `menu: boolean`. It is true when any of the last 6 cleaned, non-empty lines of the visible pane (all of them, not only the lines that matched a prompt pattern) matches CHOICE_RE `^[❯>›]?\s*\d+\.\s`, else false; null when the item failed. The client shows the y/n buttons only when `isYesNo(preview) && menu != true`, because on a numbered menu the letter + Enter would confirm the highlighted option.

## Amendment A6 (2026-10-25, FCode v1.1: coloured screen)

Applies to `GET /api/screen/:name` and `GET /api/stream/:name` (the SSE `screen` events carry the same JSON).

1. Optional query `ansi=1`.
   - With `ansi=1` the text keeps colours: the server runs `tmux capture-pane -p -e -J -t =<name>: -S -<lines>` (`-e` added).
   - Without it, or with any other value (`ansi=0`, `ansi=true`, empty), nothing changes: the same tmux call, no escapes. Apps installed before v1.1 keep working.
2. With `ansi=1` only SGR sequences (`ESC [ <params> m`) may appear in `text`. The server removes every other escape sequence: other CSI (cursor, erase, private modes), OSC (titles, OSC 8 hyperlinks), DCS/APC/PM/SOS, two-byte `ESC x` sequences, a lone ESC, and SO/SI (0x0E, 0x0F), so the text equals a plain capture. What stays is written in one simple form that a client can parse by splitting on `;`:
   - parameters are integers separated by `;`; `ESC [ m` is sent as `ESC [ 0 m`;
   - colours are `38;5;n`, `48;5;n`, `38;2;r;g;b`, `48;2;r;g;b` (n, r, g, b in 0..255); the colon forms (`38:2::r:g:b`) are rewritten, and a cut-off one is dropped; `4:0` becomes `24`, any other `4:x` becomes `4`, `5:3` (overline) becomes `53`, any other colon group is dropped;
   - the underline colour (`58`, `59`), colours that are cut off or out of range, and codes above 107 are dropped; a sequence with nothing left is dropped.
3. Server-side text matching never sees escapes: prompt detection, the preview and the inbox/overview state work on text with escapes removed. (`/api/overview` reads the pane without `-e` and also strips any escape it meets.)
4. `hash` covers exactly the `text` that is sent (plus size and cursor, as before). With `ansi=1` a colour-only change gives a new hash, so the stream sends a new event. Trailing lines that hold only SGR and blanks count as blank and are trimmed, like trailing blank lines today.
5. tmux targets: a call that needs a pane (`capture-pane`, `display-message`, `send-keys`, `paste-buffer`, `resize-window`, `set-option`) uses `-t =<name>:`; a bare `=<name>` does not resolve a pane ("can't find pane"). Calls that need only a session (`has-session`, `kill-session`) use `-t =<name>`.

## Amendment A7 (2026-10-26, QR pairing for a new device; r2 after review)

A new device can be paired with a QR code. The QR and every link carry ONLY the server address, never a code (the `fcode://` scheme is not exclusive on iOS: another app may receive the link). The user types the 6-digit code shown on the old device or in the terminal. Nothing permanent (cookieSecret, device token) is ever in a link.
- Config: optional `publicUrl`, a bare https origin (no path, query, fragment or credentials; normalised, a trailing slash is dropped). An invalid value is a config error (startup refuses, a reload keeps the previous config). It is the ONLY source of the origin in a link: Host, X-Forwarded-Host, Forwarded and Origin are never used.
- Links: `appLink` = `fcode://pair?server=<encodeURIComponent(publicUrl)>`; `shareLink` = `<publicUrl>/pair`. No code, no name.
- The address must be one the app accepts, so the server never emits a QR that cannot work. Grammar (ONE rule shared with the iOS PairLink parser: the "rule" field and the vectors of `test/origin-vectors.json`, the same file in both trees, which both test suites load; in short): `https://` + host + optional `:port` (1-65535) + optional `/`, nothing else; ASCII only (checked before lowercasing). Host = a lowercase LDH name (labels 1-63 chars, no leading or trailing `-`, no `xn--` label, at least one dot, at most 253 chars, one trailing dot dropped, last label neither all digits nor `0x…`), or 4 decimal octets 0-255 without leading zeros, or a bracketed IPv6 address (`net.isIPv6`). Canonical form: lowercase, port 443 left out. The input is checked for printable ASCII first and then lower-cased as a whole (so `HTTPS://Box.Example.COM` is accepted); a port has no leading zero; an IPv4 with a trailing dot is rejected. `publicUrl` that loads as a URL but fails this (IDN/`xn--`, `localhost`, `_`, `192.168.001.010`, `1.2.3.0x4`…) is kept in the config but no link is made: `POST /api/pair-code` answers 500 `{error:"public_url_invalid"}` (one log line, no code made), `GET /pair` 503, and `fcode-pair --qr` prints "publicUrl trong config.json không hợp lệ cho app (cần https://tên-miền-ASCII)" to stderr and exits 1 without making a code.
- `POST /api/pair-code` {name?: string}: needs a paired device and X-PC like any other /api route (the app sends `{}`). Makes a pending code issued by the calling device and answers 200 `{code, expiresAt (ISO 8601), appLink, shareLink}`. The code is the same kind as `--pair` (6 digits, TTL 120 s, single use, redeemed by POST /api/pair).
  - Errors: 400 invalid (name not a string, bad JSON), 401, 403 (no X-PC), 409 `no_public_url` (no code is made).
  - The name (control and bidi characters and lone surrogates removed, cut on a code point to at most 64 UTF-16 units) becomes the device name, like `--pair [name]`.
- `GET|HEAD /pair` (no auth): a small Vietnamese HTML page with a button "Mở FCode" (the appLink) and "Chưa cài FCode? Cài file fcode.ipa trước.". The query string is ignored and never echoed; the page has no code and reads or changes no pairing state. `Cache-Control: no-store`. 503 when `publicUrl` is not configured.
- `fcode-pair [name] [--qr]` (install.sh wrapper -> `server.mjs --pair <name> [--qr]`; `--pair --qr` with no name means no name). With `--qr` it prints, in this order: the QR of the appLink (`qrencode -t ANSIUTF8`, apt package `qrencode`), "Link chia sẻ: <shareLink>", the code in big digits ("MÃ GHÉP:   4   8   2   9   1   3") and ONE line "Mã hết hạn sau N phút." (N from the TTL). Without qrencode it prints "Link mở app: <appLink>" and "cài qrencode để hiện mã QR" instead of the QR; without `publicUrl` a hint about it. Without `--qr` the output is the old two lines. The admin request `{cmd:'pair', name, links:true}` answers `links: {appLink, shareLink} | null`.
- Pending codes (changes A4's "one pending"): each records its issuer (a device id, or `shell` for the command). One pending code per issuer: a new one replaces that issuer's own. At most 3 in all; when a 4th is made the oldest DEVICE code goes, so a device never pushes the shell code out. Each has its own expiry (120 s) and attempt count; live codes are distinct. A wrong guess (also a malformed one) is one attempt against every live code; a code with 5 is gone. /api/pair limits (10/min, 30/h) are unchanged.
- A code dies with its issuer: `pair()` refuses a code whose issuing device is gone. Revoking a device (`--revoke <id>`, POST /api/logout) clears that device's pending codes; `--revoke all`, `logout?all=1` and a cookieSecret rotation clear ALL pending codes (the shell's too).
- The admin socket never lets an exception escape: a failing request answers `{ok:false, error:"internal"}`.
- v1.3.1 `fcode-new` (install.sh wrapper -> `server.mjs --new <args>`): `--projects` / `--harnesses` print one name per line (harnesses: omp, claude, codex); `<project> <harness>` creates a session through admin.sock `{cmd:"new", project, harness}` with the same code as the app's "+" (`openFresh`: name `<project>-<harness>`, then `-2`, `-3`, ... within 32 chars) and prints only the tmux session name. `{cmd:"meta"}` answers `{ok, projects, harnesses}`. Errors answer `{ok:false, error}` (`unknown_project`, `unknown_harness`, `harness_exited`, `busy`, ...); the CLI turns them into Vietnamese on stderr, empty stdout, exit 1. A request on admin.sock may take up to 20 s once read (the mutation queue and the harness check); the admin job's ctx has `admin: true`, which skips only the paired-device check of `valid(ctx)`.
- A config edit is applied before any route or admin request reads auth or pairing state, and before POST /api/pair looks up or consumes a code; a cookieSecret rotation therefore clears every pending code before the next redemption.

## Amendment A8 (2026-10-26, home screen v2: quota, spend, box timer, projects, Codex reset)

Shared with the iOS worker in `contract-home-v2.md` (the Architect's copy). Server side as built:

- `GET /api/home` (auth like every /api route; GET, else 405) -> 200 `{generatedAt, box, accounts, totals, projects, updates}`, shape as in contract-home-v2.md. Each part has its own cache: quota 60 s, spend 5 min, projects 2 min, box timer and updates live. One refresh per part at a time; concurrent requests share it. Stale-while-revalidate: once a part has a value, a request past its TTL gets that value at once and the refresh runs in the background (the next request sees it). A part with no value yet is waited for at most 8 s (the parts in parallel), so the whole reply comes in under 10 s (the app gives up at 20 s); a part not ready by then is empty and fills in on a later request. A refresh that failed is retried only one TTL later (the reset listing: 60 s), not on every poll. A failing part never makes a 500: no quota yet -> `accounts: []`; quota failing after a success -> the last accounts with `stale: true`; spend failing or not ready -> `spend: null` and `totals: {spend: null, byHarness: []}`; projects not read yet -> every config project with `repo`, `branch`, `prs`, `lastRun` null and `loading: true` (a gh failure has no `loading` field; the app shows "đang đọc…" for loading, "chưa đọc được GitHub" for a failure); a gh call failing -> that project's `prs` / `lastRun` null (the app shows "chưa đọc được GitHub"); no status.json -> `updates: {}`.
- Quota: `omp usage --json` plus `omp usage reset --json` (the listing gives each account's credential id), 30 s timeout each. The listing has its own 5 min cache and is waited for at most 4 s inside a quota refresh; until a first listing succeeds the accounts have `~` ids (below). A quota value built with no listing at all is kept 15 s only (not 60 s), and the listing that then succeeds drops it, so the next GET (it waits at most 8 s) has the real ids and reset targets. FCode reads no credential file (omp's `agent.db` holds credentials and is never opened). Report <-> listing match: same provider, `accountId`, `orgId` (and email when both have one). `id` = the reset target `<provider>/<credentialId>` (e.g. `anthropic/1`, `openai-codex/4`); without a listing match `id` = `<provider>/~<8 hex>`, `resets.target` null and `spend: null` (unknown, not $0; the id changes once a listing matches). The last good listing is reused when a listing fails. `harness`: anthropic -> claude, openai-codex -> codex; other providers are not shown. Accounts in `accountsWithoutUsage` are shown with `windows: []`, `stale: true`.
  - Windows: one per omp limit that has a number (`amount.usedFraction`, or `used` in percent, or `used/limit`); a limit omp does not report is hidden. `key` = `scope.windowId` + `_<tier>` (`5h`, `7d`, `7d_fable`); `label` "5 giờ" / "7 ngày" / "7 ngày Fable" (`<n> giờ|ngày` + capitalised tier); `usedPercent` one decimal; `resetsAt` ISO or null (a window not started yet); `periodSeconds` from `durationMs`.
  - `plan`: raw `planType` / `subscriptionType` -> label (free Free, plus Plus, pro Pro, max Max, team Team, business Business, enterprise Enterprise, edu Edu; else the raw value capitalised); null when omp gives none. omp 18.12.6 gives a plan for Codex only, so Claude accounts have `plan: null`. Never branched on.
  - `stale`: omp fetched the report more than 10 min ago, or the last refresh failed. `rateLimited`: the report or account carries an error mentioning a rate limit / 429. `resets.available` = `redeemableCount` (usable now), else `availableCount`.
- Spend: local logs, read incrementally (each file from where the last scan stopped, whole lines only; a shrunk or replaced file is re-read; files not modified in 31 days skipped; a removed file dropped). Sources: omp `~/.omp/agent/sessions/**/*.jsonl` (assistant messages carry `provider`, `credentialId`, `usage`, `usage.cost.total`; `model_usage` lines too), Claude Code `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR|~/.claude/projects`, Codex `$CODEX_HOME|~/.codex/{sessions,archived_sessions}`. Tokens include cache reads and writes. Cost: the log's own (omp `usage.cost.total`, Claude `costUSD`), else the bundled price table (`PRICES` in server.mjs, LiteLLM, read 2026-10-26), else tokens only (never a guessed dollar). Table lookup: the exact model name (a date suffix dropped), else the base model only for the same-price suffixes `-codex`, `-codex-max`, `-chat`, `-chat-latest`, `-search-api`; any other variant (`-pro`, `-nano`, `-cyber`, unknown ones) has no price: its event has `usd` null and only its tokens count. Dedupe: omp `responseId`, Claude `message.id` (multi-line messages and sidechain replays), Codex session id + cumulative totals (a re-emitted snapshot and an archived copy count once). Codex child rollouts (Pane `codex_child_meta` / `CodexReplayGate`, spend.rs @442bdd7): a file whose first `session_meta` payload has `forked_from_id` or `parent_thread_id` set, `thread_source: "subagent"`, or a non-null `source.subagent` (JSON null and blank strings count as absent) replays its parent's history, its parent's `task_started` lines included. Its token_count lines only seed the delta baseline and are never counted (the parent's file counts them) until the first `task_started` whose `started_at` is at or after that session_meta's timestamp in whole seconds; when the session_meta has no parseable timestamp, at or after the second of the task_started line itself. Only the file's first `session_meta` counts (session, account, gate), even one with no `id`; a repeated parent one is ignored.
  - Attribution: omp messages -> the account `<provider>/<credentialId>`; Codex logs -> the Codex account whose omp `accountId` equals the rollout's `creator_account_id`; everything else (Claude Code logs, omp `model_usage`) counts in the totals and its harness only.
  - Days are calendar days of config.json `timeZone` (an IANA zone, default `Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh`; an invalid one is a config error), never the process `TZ`; `daily30` = the 30 days ending today, oldest first. `weeklyEstimate` (Pane): spend logged inside the account's `7d` window (`resetsAt - periodSeconds` .. now) / (`usedPercent` / 100), only from 5 % used and when something was logged in the window; at >= 100 % the spend itself; null otherwise and for totals. Only the account's own (attributed) events count: Claude Code logs and omp `model_usage` lines use the same quota but carry no account, so with them the estimate comes out low. `usd` 4 decimals, `tokens` integers. `totals.byHarness` = usd per harness over the same 30 days as `last30` (the app's "30 ngày"), largest first.
- Box timer: `sleepsAt` = last resume + `maxRunMinutes` (480); the last resume is the start of a box run or a 30 s tick (also run on each /api/home) that came more than 90 s after the previous one. The server keeps `{resume, tick, boot}` in `PC_CONFIG_DIR/box-timer.json` (`resume`, `tick`: ms epochs; `boot`: `/proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id`, null where it does not exist), written with writePrivate (0600, atomic) on every 30 s tick and at start. At start it keeps the stored `resume` only when the stored `tick` is under 90 s old and the stored `boot` equals the current one (or both are null): a server restart on the same boot (reinstall, crash, `systemctl --user restart`). A reboot is always a new run; an instabox pause keeps the boot_id and is caught by the 90 s tick gap. An older, missing or invalid file also starts a new run (resume = now). Past the estimate -> `sleepsAt: null`. `idlePauseMinutes` 30, `cooldownMinutes` 10, `source: "estimate"`.
- Projects: per config project, `git remote get-url origin` -> `repo` owner/repo (https, ssh, scp-like, also an ssh host alias whose name contains "github"; the URL itself never leaves the server), `branch` = current branch; `gh -R <repo> pr list --state open --limit 20 --json number,title,mergeable,headRefOid,statusCheckRollup` (a token without checks access fails that query with "Resource not accessible" or HTTP 403: only then it is retried without `statusCheckRollup`; a timeout, a rate limit or any other failure is not retried), `gh -R <repo> run list --limit 100 --json workflowDatabaseId,workflowName,name,status,conclusion,createdAt,url,headSha` and `gh -R <repo> workflow list --all --json id,name,path` (one call each per refresh; workflows are told apart by id, not name; when the 100 runs hold no deploy run, one `run list --limit 1 --workflow <id>` per deploy workflow). v1.3.1: `lastRun` = the newest run of a workflow whose name or file path contains "deploy" (case-insensitive, a disabled one too; PR gates and CI never; none -> null); when the rollup is unreadable `checks` come from those runs: the runs whose `headSha` is the PR's `headRefOid`, the latest run per workflow, through the rules below (no run -> none; runs not readable -> null). gh needs `GH_TOKEN`: install.sh starts the service through `start.sh`, which takes `GH_TOKEN` alone from the instabox vault file the login shell sources (`/run/instabox/secrets/env`, in RAM), at each start; nothing is written to disk or logged. `checks`: any failed conclusion -> failure, any not completed / pending -> pending, empty -> none, else success. `mergeable`: MERGEABLE true, CONFLICTING false, else null. `lastRun.status`: not completed -> in_progress, success/neutral/skipped -> success, else failure; `workflow` = gh `workflowName`.
- v1.3.1 `projects[].git` = `{behind, ahead, dirty, branch, syncedAt, error}`, read from `~/.local/state/fcode/git-sync.json` (written by the box timer `fcode-git-sync`) at most once per /api/home reply, never cached with the projects part: `behind` = `behindDefault` and `ahead` = `aheadOfOrigin` (integers >= 0), `dirty`, `branch` (one line, 160 chars), `syncedAt` = `lastFetchAt` (ISO UTC), `error` = `error` (the box script writes no WIP backup any more; any `wip*` field of the file is ignored). A field of the wrong type is null on its own; a missing file, a broken file or a project the file does not list gives all six null (no error, nothing logged); the loading placeholders carry it too.
- v1.3.1 `openFresh` (the app's "+" with `fresh: true`, and fcode-new through admin.sock) first runs `fcode-git-sync <project>` (resolved on the PATH the server gives its tools, `~/.local/bin` first; no shell, detached and unref'd, output discarded), outside the mutation job. The open waits for it at most 8 s (so fcode-new and the app's 20 s budgets always hold), then creates the session as before. The sync only fetches and recounts for the card (behind / ahead / dirty); it never changes the checkout. The server never kills the sync: at the cap, or when the request or admin client goes away, the open just stops waiting (a cancelled open makes no session, 499) and the child ends by its own limits. One sync runs per project at a time; an open that arrives while it runs (even past an earlier open's cap) waits on the same one instead of starting another. A missing command or a non-zero exit never blocks the open: one log line `git-sync <project>: command not found | exit <n>`, and one line `git-sync <project>: not finished after 8 s, opening anyway` per sync that outlasts the cap. An open that reuses a session (no `fresh`) does not sync. Naming, the admin protocol and every other field are unchanged.
- Updates: `~/.local/state/fcode-update/status.json`, tools omp, claude and codex only (other keys ignored); `result` one of updated|current|failed, else null.
- `POST /api/codex-reset` `{accountId, requestId}` (X-PC and auth like every POST): `requestId` 8-64 of `[A-Za-z0-9-]`, else 400 `invalid`; unknown account 404 `unknown_account` (a plain 404 `not_found` means a server too old for this route); a Claude account 400 `not_allowed`; no reset target 409 `no_target`; quota unavailable 503 `unavailable`. Runs `omp usage reset <target>` (45 s timeout; omp itself accepts `openai-codex/<id>` and `codex/<id>`) and maps its one-line answer: "Reset applied" -> reset; "already redeemed" / "another omp process spent" -> already; "nothing to reset" -> nothing_to_reset; "no saved resets available" -> no_credit; anything else -> error with a specific Vietnamese message (login expired, reset in progress, listing failed, offer changed, omp not runnable, not confirmed). omp killed at the 45 s timeout -> error "not confirmed" (the redeem may have gone out). 200 `{result, message}`.
  - Slow reset: omp can take up to 45 s (its own 10 s listing and 15 s redeem, then the server's kill), the app waits 20 s. A reset still running after 15 s is answered 202 `{result: "pending", message: "Reset vẫn đang chạy trên box. Xem lại Hạn mức sau ít phút."}` and finishes in the background. The app treats 202 pending, 409 `in_progress` and its own timeout as final (no retry) and reloads /api/home.
  - Lock: one reset per account at a time; another `requestId` for that account meanwhile -> 409 `{error: "in_progress"}` (the app shows "reset đang chạy"); the same `requestId` joins the running one (and gets 202 pending again if it still runs after 15 s). Only a final answer (reset, already, nothing_to_reset, no_credit) is kept for its `requestId` for 15 min and given again without running omp (omp mints its own redeem id; the app's id is the server-side retry key). An error (any of the messages above, the kill included) is not kept: a retry with the same `requestId` runs omp again, which is safe because omp fences its own spend per account.
  - Every finished omp run (any answer, a background one after 202 too) drops the quota cache and the listing cache, and a quota refresh that started before is discarded. The next GET /api/home then waits (at most 8 s) for fresh numbers instead of serving the old ones; until they come it gets the old accounts marked `stale: true`.
  - Reset counts after a reset: `resets.available` comes from the listing, so after a reset it is trusted only from a listing fetched after it. The server records when the last reset finished (`lastResetAt`); each cached value carries the time its refresh started, and a refresh that a later clear dropped is never fresh and has no start time. While the stored listing is older than the last reset, a quota refresh waits up to 10 s (omp's own listing timeout) for a new one instead of 4 s. Trust goes by the listing's age only: a quota refresh marks its accounts `stale: true` and keeps its value for 15 s only, not 60 s, only while it has no kept listing started at or after `lastResetAt` (slow, failed, or dropped by a second reset), so an old count is never shown as current; the next refresh tries again (a failed listing is retried after 60 s). Once such a listing is stored, a quota value built from it is not stale and is kept 60 s as usual, even when a later listing refresh fails: a listing failure then behaves exactly as when no reset ever happened. No shared flag: two resets close together cannot make an older listing count as fresh.
  - Log line: `codex-reset <accountId> <result>` only.
- `PATCH /api/sessions/<name>` `{name: "<new>"}` renames a session (auth and X-PC like every mutation): `tmux rename-session -t =<old> <new>` (exact match), run as a mutation job, so it is ordered against every create of the server; a name taken by a session made outside the server meanwhile is refused by tmux. Errors: 400 `bad_name` (the new name fails NAME_RE or is not a string), 400 `invalid` (the old name fails NAME_RE), 404 `not_found`, 409 `name_taken`, 409 `reserved_name` (the new name is `<project>-<harness>` of a config project, the name POST /api/open reuses, and the session is not of that project and harness; iOS message: "Tên này dành cho phiên <project> · <harness> mở từ dự án. Chọn tên khác."); renaming to the same name is 200. After a rename, a stream on the old name ends with `gone {reason: "session"}` as for a closed session (the app reloads its list). Reply 200 `{name: "<new>"}`. The server keeps no per-session state by name (drafts and read marks are in the app; `@pc_project` / `@pc_harness` move with the tmux session).

## Amendment A11 (2026-10-26, v1.3.2: "Thêm dự án" from the app)

Shared with the iOS worker in `add-project-contract.md` and `add-project-contract-v2.md` (the Architect's copies). Server side as built:

- `POST /api/projects` `{repo, name?}` (X-PC and auth like every mutation; a body that is not a JSON object is 400, a wrong Content-Type 415; GET is 405). `repo` is a GitHub link or `owner/repo`: `https://[www.]github.com/o/r`, `github.com/o/r`, `git@github.com:o/r.git` (host case-insensitive), then any `/`, `.git`, `?query`, `#fragment` and extra path (`/tree/main`) is dropped; any other host, `http://`, a user or port in the URL, or `owner/repo/extra` written plain is 400 `bad_repo`. The reduced text must match `^[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+/[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+$` with neither part only dots (after one trailing `.git`, any case), else 400 `bad_repo`. `name` is optional (missing, null and "" all mean the lower-cased repo part); a typed one is lower-cased and loses a trailing `.git`; it must match `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]{0,63}$` and not be `home`, else 400 `bad_name` (not a string, or a control character, too). No control character anywhere (`bad_repo` / `bad_name`). The repo is judged before the name. Nothing is trimmed: a space or newline around the text is refused.
- Answer 202 `{job}` (32 hex). The job runs `fcode-add.sh <owner/repo> <name>`: `bash <dir of server.mjs>/fcode-add.sh` (install.sh copies `box/fcode-add.sh` there; a checkout runs `box/fcode-add.sh`), spawned with an argument array and no shell, stdin closed, stdout read for `R <CODE> [detail]` lines, stderr dropped, `FCODE_CFG` = this server's config.json, in its own process group. One running job per NAME: a POST for that name (any repo) while its job runs is 202 with the SAME job id and starts nothing; two POSTs at once start one run. Another name runs in parallel. A job lives in memory only: 30 min after it ends it is 404 (a running job is never dropped), and a server restart forgets all jobs (the box script itself is safe to run again).
- `GET /api/projects/jobs/<id>` -> 200 `{state: "running"|"done"|"failed", code, name, repo, via, pubkey?, keyUrl?, detail}`; unknown id 404 `no_job`. `code` null while running. `via`: `"key"` when the script printed KEY_NEW or KEY_EXISTS (the deploy-key route ended the run, also after a token run that fell back), else `"token"` when it printed TOKEN_OK, else null (running, or it stopped before choosing). `pubkey` and `keyUrl` (`https://github.com/<repo>/settings/keys/new`) only for NEED_KEY and NEED_WRITE, and only when the script's PUBKEY line is exactly `ssh-ed25519 <base64> [comment]`: anything else is dropped (a private key can never pass). `detail` is null or one clean line of at most 200 characters (control characters and escapes removed, `ghp_`-style and `github_pat_` tokens replaced by `<token>`, `//user:pass@` in a URL by `//<cred>@`), taken from the script's SSH_DETAIL, CLONE_FAIL, DIR_EXISTS, DIR_UNSAFE, HOOK_FAIL, URL_REWRITE, CRED_FAIL, CFG_CONFLICT, CFG_BROKEN or CLEANUP_FAIL line (the first one present); never for exit 0.
- Exit code -> state and code: 0 done ADDED; 30 done ADDED_WARN (detail = the CLEANUP_FAIL branch when there is one); 40 failed NEED_KEY; 41 NEED_WRITE; 42 WRITE_BLOCKED; 43 NET_FAIL; 44 REPO_ARCHIVED; 11 DIR_CONFLICT; 21 CFG_CONFLICT (but 21 with an `R ALIAS_FAIL` line, the ssh config could not be written, is FAILED); 22 CFG_BROKEN; 23 NAME_USED; 2 BAD_ARGS; 12 CLONE_FAIL; anything else, a signal or a script that cannot start FAILED. After 10 minutes the job is failed TIMEOUT at once and its whole process group gets SIGTERM; on Linux timeout(1) kills what is left 30 s later (`--kill-after`, `PC_ADD_KILL_AFTER_S`), and the server's own SIGKILL backstop comes only at +45 s (the script's TERM trap removes its clone, which can take a while). Closing the app sends SIGTERM to every running group.
- The log holds only `add-project <name> <CODE>`; the token, the private key, the config text and gh's output are never logged or returned. `PC_ADD_SCRIPT` (test-only, like PC_GH) is a command, one path or a JSON array `["cmd","arg",...]`, in place of the bash script.
- After a project is added (the script rewrites config.json by rename) the next request sees it in `/api/home`, `/api/overview` and `/api/meta`: the config reload that every route runs first now also drops the cached home project list when the `projects` object changed, so the new card shows at once (before this, up to 2 min). The home reply is built from `cfg.projectNames` in config order: each project comes from the cached list by name, a project the cache does not know yet is a `loading: true` placeholder, a removed one is gone. After such a change the next `/api/home` does not wait for the list refresh at all (the refresh runs in the background), so the new project is in the FIRST reload after the add (loading), and filled in on a later one.
- `GET /api/github/repos` (auth; GET else 405) -> 200 `{repos: [{repo, private, archived, canPush, updatedAt, onBox}]}` (`canPush` is GitHub's `permissions.push`: the user's role on the repo, a hint only. The box's token can still be refused when the project is added; the add then falls back to a deploy key) sorted by `updatedAt` descending (null last), at most 300. Source: `gh api "/user/repos?affiliation=owner,collaborator,organization_member&sort=updated&per_page=100&page=N" --jq '.[] | {...} | @json'` for N = 1, 2, 3 in turn, stopping at the first page with fewer than 100 entries (never `--paginate`: an account with thousands of repos cannot run out of time; `sort=updated` makes the first 300 the newest), one JSON object per line (a bad line is skipped; flags that are not `true` are false), 30 s timeout per page, a failing page is a failure of the whole list, the gh result cached 60 s and shared by concurrent requests (a failure is not cached). `onBox` is the config project whose `git remote get-url origin` names that repo (lower-cased owner/name, any URL form that GET /api/home accepts, the first project in config order); it is read on every request, never cached, so a project just added shows at once. No usable login (gh missing, exit 4, "gh auth login", `GH_TOKEN`, 401 or "Bad credentials") -> 200 `{repos: [], reason: "no_github_token"}`; any other gh failure -> 502 `{error: "github_unavailable"}`. gh's output is never returned.
- `box/fcode-add.sh` is the one source of the add logic (the laptop's `fcode add` will call the installed copy later). Token route first: when `gh api repos/<repo> --jq .permissions.push` prints `true` (20 s limit), `FCODE_NO_TOKEN` is unset, it prints `R TOKEN_OK` and `R READ_OK`, clones `https://github.com/<repo>.git` with `-c credential.helper= -c credential.helper='!gh auth git-credential'` (the empty value resets inherited helpers), then writes the same chain into the repo's own config, an empty `credential.helper` first and the gh helper second (never global, no token in a URL or file), and runs the same hook, write check, config and verify steps as the key route. `permissions.push` is only a first filter: GitHub reports the user's role, not the token's scope (seen on the box: `push` true, then the HTTPS push got 403 "Permission to ... denied"), so the REAL write check decides: a push made by THIS run with THIS credential, never an existing ref and never a failed delete (see "A11 update r2"). If the token cannot clone (not a network error) or that write check is refused for permission (stderr "Permission to ... denied", "Write access to repository not granted", "marked as read only", `returned error: 401/403`, "Authentication failed", "could not read Username ... terminal prompts disabled"), it prints `R TOKEN_FALLBACK`, removes its own clone (a folder that was there before is never adopted: see A11 update r3), removes its temp file, releases its lock and re-runs itself with `FCODE_NO_TOKEN=1` (that run clones again): the deploy-key route (KEY_*, ALIAS_*, NEED_KEY / NEED_WRITE) then decides. Net errors (ssh and curl wording), an archived repo and a protected-branch refusal are final on the token route (43, 44, 42). Exit codes and the other `R` lines are unchanged. Tests: `test/fcode-add.test.mjs` runs the real script with a local bare repo as GitHub (git `url.<base>.insteadOf`), a fake `gh`, throwaway `FCODE_SSH_DIR` / `FCODE_WORKSPACE` / `FCODE_CFG`, plus the server running it.

### A11 update r2 (2026-10-26, review round 1 of the add-project branch)

- Write proof (box/fcode-add.sh). The check pushes ONE probe branch that only this run knows: `refs/heads/box/fcode-add-check-<name with [^a-z0-9-] as ->-<epoch>-<pid>-<random>` (suffix `[a-z0-9-]+`; the app shows this exact branch in its ADDED_WARN text), made from an empty-tree commit of this run, created with `--force-with-lease=<ref>:` (it must not exist yet) and deleted with `--force-with-lease=<ref>:<that commit>` (only its own commit). An existing branch, an "up to date" answer or a failed delete is never proof. Once the create has succeeded the write is proven; ANY refused delete (permission, archived, network, other) is only `CLEANUP_FAIL <that exact branch>` (ADDED_WARN). A TERM between the create and the delete also leaves the branch (its name is unique): accepted. Two runs on one repo under different names touch only their own probe. The old fixed `box/fcode-add-check` name is not used any more.
- Hook. Installation errors (hooks folder, file, mode, config) end the run with `R HOOK_FAIL install`, exit 24 (the server reports FAILED) before the project is registered. The clone's own `core.hooksPath` is set to its real hooks folder (repo-local), so a global or system `core.hooksPath` cannot bypass it, and the hook is verified the way git uses it: `git push --dry-run` of an empty-tree commit to `main` against a throw-away local bare repository must be refused with the hook's message, and the same to `box/x` must go through (`R HOOK_FAIL verify`, exit 24, otherwise). Running the hook file directly proves nothing and is not done. The same check gives `V_HOOK_OK` / `V_HOOK_BAD` after the project is added.
- Paths. Before anything changes, a target that is a symlink, a folder whose resolved path is not exactly `<resolved workspace>/<name>`, or whose `.git` is a symlink or whose resolved git dir is not `<folder>/.git`, is refused: `R DIR_UNSAFE unsafe`, exit 11 (DIR_CONFLICT). Any other existing folder is `R DIR_EXISTS exists`, exit 11 (A11 update r3). The workspace itself may be a symlink.
- Cleanup. The clone this run made is removed on any failure before the project is registered in config.json (hook, write check, NEED_WRITE, WRITE_BLOCKED, ARCHIVED, a failing registration) and on TERM / INT / HUP; a folder that existed before the run is never removed; after registration it is never removed. The `R` lines are written with SIGPIPE ignored, so a server that went away does not kill a running add midway. The mktemp file is removed before the TOKEN_FALLBACK re-exec (EXIT traps do not run on exec). The read-only alias-owner and key-owner checks (NAME_USED, exit 23) now run before the token route, so a fallback that would end in NAME_USED never leaves a clone.
- Durability. config.json and its `.bak-*` copy are written, flushed and fsynced before `os.replace`, and the folder is fsynced after it.
- Job lifecycle (server.mjs). On Linux the script runs under `timeout --kill-after=30 <deadline>` (`PC_ADD_KILL_AFTER_S` overrides the 30, test-only) (the same 10 minutes as the server's own timer; the code 124 maps to TIMEOUT; after --kill-after the group is killed and the server sees a signal, never a code 137), so the deadline holds when the server is gone. `main()` handles SIGTERM and SIGINT: `app.close()` (which sends SIGTERM to every running job group, and the script then cleans up and exits 143), then exit 0 (hard exit after 5 s). `KillMode=process` in install.sh is kept on purpose (tmux sessions must survive a restart); after a crash or SIGKILL the job is not killed, and ends by its own `timeout`; its output pipe is gone, which the script survives (SIGPIPE ignored); the server forgets the job (a poll answers 404 `no_job`, and a retry of the same repo and name is safe). Jobs are pruned on every submit as well as on every poll: ended ones after 30 min, and at most 50 are kept, the oldest finished first (a running job is never dropped). `PC_ADD_TIMEOUT_MS` (test-only) overrides the deadline.

### A11 update r3 (2026-10-26, review round 2: existing folders are no longer adopted)

- **A folder that already exists is never adopted; pick another name or remove it on the box.** If `<workspace>/<name>` exists in any form (directory, file, symlink, git or not), the script refuses before any change: `R DIR_EXISTS exists` (exit 11; the job code stays DIR_CONFLICT, detail `exists`), or `R DIR_UNSAFE unsafe` (exit 11, detail `unsafe`) when it is a symlink, resolves outside the workspace, or its `.git` is a link or a git dir elsewhere. The reuse path (CLONE_EXISTS, set-url on an existing clone, an inherited pushurl / insteadOf / hooksPath / credential config) is gone: every later check runs on a clone made by this run. The one exception is an already registered project: the config maps `<name>` to this folder and its `remote.origin.url` names the same repo (any URL form): the script prints `R CFG_EXISTS` and exits 0, and touches nothing (no gh call, no write check, no config or credential change). The job is then done ADDED, with `via` null.
- Credentials. Every network git call of the token route (clone, probe push) runs `git -c credential.helper= -c credential.helper='!gh auth git-credential' ...`: the empty value resets what system or global config brings, so only gh is asked and told about a credential. The clone's own config gets the same chain (an empty `credential.helper`, then the gh helper) and a failed write of it fails the add (`R CRED_FAIL config`, exit 25, FAILED; the clone is removed).
- Push destination. The probe create and delete push to the explicit URL of the chosen route (`https://github.com/<repo>.git` or the `git@github-<name>:<repo>.git` alias), never to `origin`. Before the clone (and again on the finished clone) the script refuses a git config that rewrites that URL: a `url.*.insteadOf` or `url.*.pushInsteadOf` in the system, global, repo or worktree config whose value is a prefix of it, or a `remote.origin.pushurl` (`R URL_REWRITE rewrite`, exit 26, FAILED). Settings made through `-c` or the environment of the run itself (the test harness) are not counted. Needs git 2.26 (`--show-scope`).
- Hooks. After the clone the `.git/hooks` folder, `hooks/pre-push` and `.git` must not be symlinks and must resolve inside the clone, checked before mkdir, install and chmod (else `R HOOK_FAIL install`, exit 24; the clone is removed). The repo-local `core.hooksPath` of the A11 r2 rule stays: only a GLOBAL or system `core.hooksPath` can exist now, and the box's global hooks do not run in FCode-added clones.
- Registration vs cleanup. TERM, INT and HUP are ignored for the registration step (they are not deferred: the run goes on to its end), and the Python writer reports through `os.write` and ignores a closed output. From the `os.replace` on the project is registered: a later error (the directory fsync) is a warning (`R CFG_WARN fsync`, exit 3 inside, the run ends 30), never a failure. The cleanup that removes a clone also reads config.json first: when it already maps `<name>` to this folder (and did not before the run) the folder is not removed, whatever the exit status.
- Job detail words (server.mjs ADD_DETAIL, first line with text wins): `SSH_DETAIL`, `CLONE_FAIL`, `DIR_EXISTS` (`exists`), `DIR_UNSAFE` (`unsafe`), `HOOK_FAIL` (`install` | `verify`), `URL_REWRITE` (`rewrite`), `CRED_FAIL` (`config`), `CFG_CONFLICT`, `CFG_BROKEN`, `CLEANUP_FAIL`. The app matches: DIR_CONFLICT + `exists` (or none), DIR_CONFLICT + `unsafe`, FAILED + `install` | `verify` | `rewrite` (26) | `config` (25).
- Final R codes and exit codes of box/fcode-add.sh (for the laptop owner): exit 0 done (R CFG_EXISTS alone = already registered, nothing touched); 30 done with a warning (CLEANUP_FAIL <branch>, V_*_BAD, CFG_WARN); 40 NEED_KEY (+ SSH_DETAIL, PUBKEY); 41 NEED_WRITE (+ PUBKEY); 42 WRITE_BLOCKED; 43 NET_FAIL; 44 REPO_ARCHIVED; 11 DIR_EXISTS or DIR_UNSAFE; 12 CLONE_FAIL; 2 USAGE / BAD_ARGS; 20 KEY_FAIL; 21 CFG_CONFLICT, or ALIAS_FAIL; 22 CFG_BROKEN; 23 NAME_USED; 24 HOOK_FAIL install | verify; 25 CRED_FAIL; 26 URL_REWRITE; 143 stopped by TERM/INT/HUP (clone removed); 124 only from timeout(1). Lines: KEY_NEW, KEY_EXISTS, ALIAS_ADDED, ALIAS_EXISTS, TOKEN_OK, TOKEN_FALLBACK, READ_OK, CLONED, HOOK_OK, HOOK_EXISTS, WRITE_OK, CFG_ADDED, CFG_EXISTS, V_EMPTY_REPO, V_BRANCH_OK / V_BRANCH_BAD, V_PR_OK / V_PR_BAD, V_HOOK_OK / V_HOOK_BAD, V_SERVER_OK / V_SERVER_BAD, V_CFG_BAD, RULES_YES / RULES_NO. Gone: CLONE_EXISTS, DIR_NOTGIT, DIR_OTHER.

### A11 update r4 (2026-10-26, review round 3: atomic reservation, escalation proof)

- Reservation. Right after the existence check (before the key and alias steps) the script reserves the target with ONE atomic `mkdir "$dir"` (no `-p`): if it fails the run is `DIR_EXISTS exists` (someone else made the folder in the same instant: never touched) or, when the folder is not there, `CLONE_FAIL` with mkdir's own error (exit 12, e.g. a workspace that cannot be written). From the moment mkdir succeeds the folder is owned by this run (`owned=1`): the cleanup and the token fallback remove it on every exit before the project is registered (failed or half clone, a TERM during the clone, a hook error, NAME_USED, NEED_KEY...), never after registration. TERM, INT and HUP are held across mkdir -> owned (bash runs a trapped signal only after the foreground command returns) and honoured right after (exit 143, folder removed). The mkdir itself runs in a child with TERM, INT and HUP ignored (`( trap '' TERM INT HUP; exec mkdir "$dir" )`; SIG_IGN survives exec), so a signal sent to the whole process group (timeout(1), the server's close()) cannot kill it between mkdir(2) and its result; on the failure branch a held signal ends the run (143) without touching the folder, and a dangling symlink that appeared at the target meanwhile counts as DIR_EXISTS like any other entry. The parent folder is made with a separate `mkdir -p "$ws"`.
- Rewrite before the clone. A rewrite of the https URL found before the clone (a global `url.*.insteadOf` / `pushInsteadOf` / `remote.origin.pushurl` as in A11 r3) makes the run a deploy-key run from that point: no `TOKEN_OK`, no `TOKEN_FALLBACK`, no re-exec. The key URL is checked the same way (`URL_REWRITE`, exit 26, if it is rewritten too); on the key route a rewrite is 26 at once; after the clone a rewrite is 26 on both routes.
- Lifecycle invariant. Every child of the script is waited for before the script goes on (a trapped signal runs only after the foreground command returns) or is bounded on its own: the process substitution in `url_rewrite_check` is a local `git config` read to EOF; `timeout 20 gh ...` (the permission probe and `gh pr list`) runs in its own process group with its own limit. The job's deadline is timeout(1)'s TERM then KILL to the process group, proven by the escalation tests (a TERM-ignoring job and grandchild must die within the bound; without `--kill-after` they do not); a TERM from the server's `close()` is forwarded by timeout(1), which arms the same KILL. The script must not use `&`, `nohup`, `setsid`, `disown`, `coproc` or a process substitution that is not read to EOF.
- `gh pr list` in the final verification also runs under `timeout 20` (a hang is V_PR_BAD, not a stuck job).
- Not covered (out of scope): a folder left by a hard KILL after kill-after or by a power loss in the middle of the clone (remove it on the box: `rm -rf /data/workspace/<name>`); a box hook or helper that daemonizes a TERM-ignoring process.
